messages:
lina-cs: FYI customer acme reported a sudden drop in answer quality right after last night's rollout. They see short, vague replies and more hallucinations on product-descriptions endpoint. Attaching their minimal repro and request IDs.

lina-cs: Quote from customer: "After the update our product descriptions went from specific specs to generic fluff — example: asked 'battery life' and got 'long-lasting' with no numbers'. They gave a few request IDs: req_8a3f, req_8b1c, req_8f22.

ravi-eng: thanks — can you paste one of the full request payloads (headers + body) and the model name/version? Also which region/route were they hitting?

lina-cs: pasted below. They hit us-east-1 on route `/v1/generate`. Model: redwood-draft-sampler-v2.1. Request: ```{\n  "model":"redwood-draft-sampler-v2.1",\n  "input":"Write a product description: 36V ebike battery capacity and typical range.",\n  "temperature":0.7,\n  "max_tokens":120,\n  "speculative_decoding":true\n}```

ravi-eng: ah ok speculative_decoding=true. Ops bot shows rollout of `redwood-draft-sampler-v2.1` at 2026-03-16T23:12:02Z to hosted/us-east-1 (canary 10% => 100%). Do we have perf/quality metrics from the eval suite for this rollout?

ops-bot: Deploy: redwood-draft-sampler-v2.1 promoted to hosted/us-east-1 at 2026-03-16T23:12:02Z by tim-prod. Canary -> 100%. Change notes: "speculative sampler improvements, reduced KV pressure".

nora-ml: I ran a quick diff on our internal evals — the draft sampler increases token diversity but at cost of precision on short factual queries (battery life, specs). Looks like temperature/decoding heuristics combined with the speculative path are causing the sampler to prefer generic safe tokens in low-context prompts.

ravi-eng: Thanks. Immediate triage steps: 1) reproduce locally with same payload and `speculative_decoding=true`. 2) flip `speculative_decoding=false` to confirm it's the source. 3) collect `x-request-id` and server logs for those req IDs, and full model trace (kv cache hits, fallback counts). Lina can you ask the customer for the `x-request-id` headers for req_8a3f etc?

lina-cs: asked customer for headers/trace ids. Meanwhile I tried a local curl with the same prompt. Repro'd the generic answer. Ran again with `speculative_decoding:false` and got the previous, more factual style.

ravi-eng: Good repro. Can you share the curl snippet you used so we can replicate in staging?

lina-cs: Here it is:
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \\n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \\n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \\n  -d '{"model":"redwood-draft-sampler-v2.1","input":"Write a product description: 36V ebike battery capacity and typical range.","temperature":0.7,"max_tokens":120,"speculative_decoding":true}'
```

nora-ml: Ok hypothesis: the speculative path uses a lightweight scorer that nudges towards tokens with higher model-ensemble uncertainty; for short factual prompts this increases vagueness. Fix options: revert speculative path globally, introduce a heuristic to disable it for <n token input/low-req-context, or tighten the sampler's temperature/bias for the speculative scorer.

tim-prod: We should avoid broad rollback unless necessary. Suggest immediate mitigation: patch gateway to ignore speculative_decoding header for hosted routes where customer profile flagged 'strict-factual' or when prompt matches short/spec query heuristics. Can we do a quick feature-flag rollback for hosted/us-east-1?

ravi-eng: I can flip a runtime flag to disable speculative decoding globally in us-east-1 for now, takes ~5m to propagate. Doing it if we get customer confirmation that turning it off restores quality.

ops-bot: Action scheduled: runtime flag `enable_speculative_decoding` -> false in hosted/us-east-1. Started change at 1934567950.

lina-cs: Customer confirmed: they tested with `speculative_decoding=false` and quality restored. Please proceed with any mitigations.

ravi-eng: Flag now false in us-east-1. Monitoring outputs and sampling metrics. Initial sanity check: token-level entropy decreased, factual answer rate on our sanity prompts returned to baseline.

nora-ml: I'll open an ML issue to tune the speculative scorer and add a regression test on our factual prompt set. Recommend we also add an opt-in alpha for customers to try improved sampler once we have calibrated heuristics.

tim-prod: I'll draft a customer-facing note and coordinate a follow-up with acme. Good work team. :thumbsup:

lina-cs: Notifying customer and closing the escalation for now. Will re-open if they see more issues. Thanks all.
